PullRequest.Title: Allow comment width to always be resized

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening, restoring, or resetting a floating comment thread widget
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget measures editor/content widths, computes the default or restored width, applies width/height, and renders before placement is visible. The diff adds a cached local for the already-required width measurement plus constant-time range/default-width calculations; it does not add another DOM measurement or asynchronous dependency.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One sizing pass per shown/reset widget; occupied-rectangle placement still scales with the number of other visible floating comment widgets, but that unchanged host scan is not increased by this diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI work on the renderer event path, one widget sizing operation at a time; no new queue, burst, or parallel work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Stored layouts remain in the existing bounded 500-entry LRU cache. Cold widgets compute a default layout; warm widgets restore a layout and apply the same single width measurement as before. The diff does not change keys, misses, invalidation, or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing _computeDefaultLayout, _applySize, _measureContentWidths, and the host layout cache. The only new work is pure arithmetic, including a duplicate pure getWidthRange calculation inside getDefaultWidth.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual DOM layout cost varies with thread complexity, but the changed code does not increase measurement cardinality: content widths are measured once in the default-layout path before and after the PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Initial width behavior changes, but synchronous DOM reads, writes, comment layout calls, and render count are not materially increased.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dragging a floating comment widget resize sash horizontally or from a corner
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ResizableHTMLElement emits one resize event per sash movement; _onResize clamps width, lays out the comment thread when width changes, measures heights, and renders. The PR broadens the permitted maximum width from natural content width to editor width but does not add events, measurements per event, or a boundary call.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with pointer-move events during an intentional resize and with rendered comment-thread complexity. The user can now continue changing width over a larger range, so more moves may perform actual layout instead of clamping, but that work is the direct requested interaction and remains bounded by editor width and event count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous, serial pointer-event handling with one active resize session; no parallelism, background work, limiter, IPC, or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The width range is captured once at resize start. No cache or coalescing behavior changes; content-layout calls remain skipped when computed content width is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing ResizableHTMLElement.onDidChange through _onWillResize, _onResize, _setWidth, _measureContentHeights, and _render.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser layout cost depends on comment DOM size and pointer frequency. The wider interactive range can cause additional expected relayout while actively dragging, but there is no realistic evidence of a material regression beyond the feature's required resize updates.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance finding. The broader resize range is intentional, editor-bounded, user-driven, and does not change per-event work or event fan-out enough to establish a concrete regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Comment content changes while a floating widget is already wider than its natural content
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A content-size event synchronously calls _applySize and _render. The new width range preserves a user-selected width up to editor width rather than clamping it to natural content; the same width/height measurements and render operations occur as before.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One apply/render pass per existing content-size event; cost scales with comment DOM complexity, not with the newly allowed width itself.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial renderer event handling; no new scheduling, batching, or concurrency behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The in-memory chosen layout and existing _contentLayoutWidth guard are unchanged. Warm updates avoid CommentThreadWidget.layout when the applied content width is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing onDidChangeContentSize to _onContentSizeChanged and _applySize.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM geometry cost varies by thread, but the diff changes the allowed value rather than the number of content-size events or geometry reads.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; preserving the wider chosen size does not introduce repeated work, unbounded retention, or an expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced initial sizing, restored sizing, content updates, and interactive resize handling. No changed subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, network, or serialization boundaries are reachable. The PR changes width policy while preserving DOM measurement and event cardinality, so no high-confidence actionable performance issue was found.
